title: Systems of Linear Inequalities
seo_title: Algebra I Systems of Linear Inequalities Worksheets (TEKS A.3H)
standard_text: A.3H graph the solution set of systems of two linear inequalities in two variables on the coordinate plane; A.2H write linear inequalities in two variables given a table of values, a graph, and a verbal description
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.3H and A.2H: test points, read graphs of systems of inequalities, write systems and solve problems in context. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A point must make every inequality true.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Graph each inequality. The solutions are where the shadings overlap.
  • A point is a solution only if it makes every inequality true.
  • Points on a dashed line are not solutions.

Examples

Example

Is (1, 2) a solution of y > x and y ≤ 3?

2 > 1 true

2 ≤ 3 true

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Checking only one inequalityTest both.
Shading outside the overlapOnly the overlap is the solution.
Counting points on a dashed lineDashed means not included.

sets.title: Write a system and read graphs

items.q: Why are x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0 often included in a real-world system?
c: Because every system needs four inequalities
Amounts like hours or items cannot be negative
items.e: You cannot work −3 hours or buy −2 items, so the amounts cannot be negative.

items.q: Which phrase means <?
items.e: Fewer than 10 means less than 10, not including 10.

items.q: Ava earns $15 an hour tutoring and $10 an hour at the café, and wants to earn at least $240. Which inequality shows this?
items.e: “At least” means ≥: 15x + 10y ≥ 240.

items.q: A school club sells pizza slices (p) for $3 and cookies (c) for $1. It needs more than $150. Which inequality fits?
items.e: “More than” means >: 3p + c > 150.

items.q: A theater has 300 seats. Adult tickets (a) cost $10 and child tickets (c) cost $6. It needs at least $2,400 in sales. Which system fits?
items.e: Seats: at most 300. Money: at least $2,400. a + c ≤ 300 and 10a + 6c ≥ 2,400.

items.q: Which phrase means ≥?
items.e: At least 5 means 5 or more: ≥.

items.q: Grace needs at least 3 servings of fruit (f) and vegetables (v) together, but no more than 2 servings of fruit. Which system fits?
items.e: Together at least 3 → ≥ 3; fruit no more than 2 → f ≤ 2.

items.q: A van holds no more than 12 people: a adults and k kids. There must be at least 2 adults. Which system fits?
items.e: No more than 12 → ≤ 12; at least 2 adults → a ≥ 2.

items.q: Ava works at most 20 hours a week at two jobs: x hours tutoring and y hours at a café. Which inequality shows this?
items.e: “At most” means ≤: x + y ≤ 20.

items.q: A baker has 24 cups of flour. Bread uses 3 cups and muffins use 2 cups per batch. Which inequality shows the flour limit for b batches of bread and m batches of muffins?
items.e: Flour used must not be more than 24: 3b + 2m ≤ 24.

items.q: Which inequality is shown by the graph?
items.e: The boundary line is y = x + 1. It is dashed (not included), so the sign is < or >. The shading is above the line, so y > x + 1.

sets.title: Systems in context and test points

items.q: For x + y ≤ 20 and 15x + 10y ≥ 240, can Ava work 4 hours tutoring and 14 at the café?
c: No, the hours are too many
items.e: 4 + 14 = 18 ≤ 20 ✓, but 60 + 140 = 200, which is less than 240: she earns too little.

items.q: Which point is on the boundary but NOT a solution of y < x + 1?
items.e: 3 = 2 + 1, so (2, 3) is on the dashed line, which is not included: (2, 3).

items.q: To graph 2x + y > 4, it is easiest to first rewrite it as…
items.e: Subtract 2x from both sides: y > −2x + 4.

items.q: How do you test which side of y ≥ −x + 3 to shade?
c: Test a point like (0, 0) in the inequality
items.e: 0 ≥ 3 is false, so shade the side without (0, 0). Testing a point always works.

items.q: For x + y ≤ 20 and 15x + 10y ≥ 240, can Ava work 12 hours tutoring and 6 at the café?
c: No, the hours are too many

items.q: To graph −y ≤ x − 1, Ethan writes y ≤ −x + 1. What is the correct inequality?
items.e: Dividing by −1 reverses the sign: y ≥ −x + 1.

items.q: Which inequality has a solid boundary and shading below the line?
items.e: ≤ gives a solid line and shading below: y ≤ 3x − 2.

items.q: Which point is in the solution region of y > 2x and y < 5?
items.e: 4 > 2 ✓ and 4 < 5 ✓: (1, 4). (1, 2) fails because 2 is not greater than 2.

items.q: A van system is a + k ≤ 12 and a ≥ 2. Which group can go?
items.e: 3 + 9 = 12 ≤ 12 and 3 ≥ 2: 3 adults and 9 kids.

items.q: A system is y > 2x + 1 and y < 2x − 3. How many solutions does it have?
items.e: The lines are parallel; one shading is above the higher line and the other below the lower line, so they never overlap: none.
